Traupman 109: accipe, em

Em!

here!, handing something over

Other words

  • Ecce tibi … — here is … for you (handing something over)

    also used · modern · Traupman 113: Ecce tibi decem dollarōs, here are your ten dollars

    Classically ecce tibi introduces something new and unexpected, “and look, here comes …” (ecce tibi exortus est Isocratēs, Cic. de Or. 2.22 fin., Lewis & Short s.v. ecce). Handing over money with it is Traupman’s use; Em! or Accipe says it in the comic way.

  • Ecce. — here it is, there you are

    interjection, with a nominative or alone · also used · classical · Plaut. (Lewis & Short): quem quaerō, optimē ecce obviam mihi est; Traupman 25: Ecce., here it is

    Points at something: “look!, here!”; handing a thing over, em is the comic word.

Examples

  • Accipe, em.

    here, take itcomposed

  • Em manum!

    here’s my handcomposed

  • «Accipe, em. Ita tenē: laeva ministeriō, dextra est intenta labōrī.»

    “Here, take it. Hold it like this: the left hand helps, the right does the work.”Libellus IV, Diēs Grātulātiōnis

See also give it here!, careful, don’t fall.
